overview: Evaluation of public transport, non-motorised transport (NMT), road infrastructure, IPT/paratransit, metro rail, and personalised vehicles; reviews trends, challenges, ongoing initiatives, and provides recommendations.
current_situation: Public transport = 9.42% of trips (vs. 40-50% URDPFI benchmark); walking 25.29%, cycling 0.80%; 67% of motorised trips are private, 33% public/IPT. 27,08,550 registered vehicles as of March 2025 (ESR); ~101 vehicles per 100 residents (RTO data). Two-wheelers = 66% of vehicles (RTO)/71% (ESR); cars 22%/20%. Vehicle registrations growing ~23%/year. ~70% of vehicles are BS-4 or older emission standard.

baseline_data.metric: MoHUA benchmark buses per lakh population

challenges: Steep increase in private vehicles and vehicular pollution (46% of PM2.5 from transport per SAFAR-Pune 2020; 91% increase 2012-2019)
Low public-transport supply vs. MoHUA benchmark (23 vs. 60 buses/lakh)
Bus ridership has not exceeded pre-COVID 10.5 lakh/day level for 2-3 years
Growing traffic congestion on major corridors
Freight movement near industrial zones adds congestion and delays
existing_initiatives: Harit Setu - Connected Greens masterplan (2022) - connects new metro lines, BRTS, and railway station
Comprehensive Mobility Plan for PCMC (2008, 2018) and for PMR (2025)
Non-Motorised Transport Policy for Pimpri Chinchwad (2021)
Pimpri Chinchwad City Electric Vehicle Readiness Plan (2023)
ICCT & ITDP Low Emission Zone study (2023)
Road Asset Management System (RAMS) for data management
Pothole Management System for transparent, scientific repairs

strategies.name: Raise public transport share (buses+metro) from 12.75% to 50% by 2050; speed shift of PT fleets to cleaner fuels.
Boost walking and cycling trips from 26% to 50% by 2040 by developing safe, healthy, accessible complete streets.
Encourage transition to clean, efficient urban freight movement while minimising citywide freight congestion (Urban Logistics Reforms).
Facilitate private-vehicle transitions to cleaner fuels (CNG, EV) with effective parking management.
Implement a phased Low Emission Zone: BS-IV/VI restrictions in Priority-1 area by 2026, citywide by 2032, low-emission-only citywide by 2040.
Establish a comprehensive, real-time data management system for evidence-based mobility planning.
Enhance institutional capacity and citizen engagement through awareness campaigns, training, events.
